metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (VB.NET code-behind) with a deployable entry point (ASP.NET WebForms page served by IIS), backed by a database connection string pointing to SQL Server.
metadata.archetype_justification: The application performs CRUD operations on a timesheets database table (INSERT and SELECT operations via SqlCommand), stores user-specific data (employee_id from Session), and exposes both read and write endpoints.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.18 falls in the Not Ready band (< 1.5), but 11 High findings yield Remediation Required tier (2-11 High). The count-based tier requires >= 12 High findings to reach Not Ready. The score band more accurately reflects the system's deep modernization gaps across all categories.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: The application is too small (single VB.NET code-behind, single CRUD operation) to decompose into microservices. The correct path is a rewrite in a modern stack deployed on managed infrastructure.
decomposition_strategy.effort_estimate: Low to Medium for rewrite, Medium for DevOps foundation

findings.title: All compute on end-of-life IIS 6 / Windows Server 2003
findings.description: All compute runs on a single IIS 6 instance on Windows Server 2003. No managed container orchestration, no serverless. OS and web server are end-of-life with no security patches available.
findings.gap: No managed compute services. Running on unsupported, unpatched operating system and web server.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed compute — containerize on ECS/Fargate after rewriting to .NET 6+, or adopt Lambda for the API layer.

findings.title: Self-managed SQL Server 2005 on-premises
findings.description: Database is self-managed SQL Server 2005 at IP 10.0.6.15. No managed database services. Engine is 10+ years past EOL.
findings.gap: Entirely self-managed database on end-of-life engine. No automated failover, no managed backups, no scaling.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for SQL Server or Aurora PostgreSQL using AWS DMS.

findings.title: No workflow orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service detected. All logic is hardcoded in code-behind event handlers with no structure for workflow needs.
findings.gap: No orchestration infrastructure for any multi-step operations.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Step Functions for any multi-step operations that emerge during modernization (e.g., approval workflows).

findings.title: No async messaging or streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. State changes cannot propagate asynchronously. All operations tightly synchronous.
findings.gap: No messaging infrastructure for cross-service state propagation.
findings.recommendation: Introduce EventBridge or SNS/SQS for timesheet events when modernizing.

findings.title: No network security configuration
findings.description: No VPC, no security groups, no network segmentation. Forms authentication does not require SSL. Credentials and session cookies transmitted in the clear.
findings.gap: No network isolation, no encryption in transit, no segmentation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a VPC with private subnets. Enforce HTTPS. Apply least-privilege security groups.

findings.title: No API gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront. Application directly exposed via IIS with no throttling, WAF, or centralized auth.
findings.gap: Direct service exposure with no managed entry point.
findings.recommendation: Place an ALB or API Gateway in front of the service with AWS WAF.

findings.title: No auto-scaling
findings.description: Single IIS instance with no scaling capability. InProc session state prevents horizontal scaling.
findings.gap: No scaling capability. Single instance is both a capacity ceiling and single point of failure.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling after modernizing compute. Externalize session state.

findings.title: No backup and recovery configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration for the SQL Server database. No retention periods, no PITR, no documented recovery procedure.
findings.gap: No automated backups. Data loss risk is unmitigated.
findings.recommendation: After migrating to RDS, automated backups with retention are included. Enable PITR.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or any IaC tool. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. Infrastructure cannot be reproduced, versioned, or audited.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in CDK or CloudFormation.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is manual Visual Studio publish to a network share.
findings.gap: No build automation, no test automation, no deployment automation.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD with CodePipeline + CodeBuild with build, test, and deploy stages.

findings.title: VB.NET on .NET Framework 2.0 — incompatible with AWS SDK
findings.description: VB.NET on .NET Framework 2.0 with ASP.NET WebForms. Runtime is incompatible with any version of the AWS SDK. No cloud-native tooling available.
findings.gap: Language runtime cannot run AWS SDK. No cloud integration path without a rewrite.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in modern .NET (C# on .NET 8+) with ASP.NET Core for first-class AWS SDK v3 support.

findings.title: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries
findings.description: Single code-behind file with UI event handlers directly executing SQL queries. No separation of concerns, no layers, no interfaces.
findings.gap: No modularity. UI, business logic, and data access interleaved in a single file.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite with clear separation: API layer, domain layer, data layer. See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: All communication synchronous with no async patterns
findings.description: All communication is synchronous. Synchronous SqlCommand calls, synchronous DataAdapter.Fill. No message publishing, no event-driven patterns.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous. State changes do not propagate to other systems.
findings.recommendation: Implement async database calls and publish timesheet events to EventBridge/SNS.

findings.title: No async job processing capability
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No background workers, no status polling, no callback patterns.
findings.gap: No async job processing. No capacity for operations exceeding 30 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Implement background job processing with SQS + Lambda workers or Step Functions.

findings.title: No API versioning strategy
findings.description: Single unversioned WebForms page. No URL versioning, no header versioning. Any change is a breaking change.
findings.gap: No versioning mechanism. No migration path for consumers on API changes.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-based versioning (e.g., /api/v1/timesheets) when rewriting.

findings.title: Hard-coded database endpoint (IP address)
findings.description: Database connection string hard-coded in web.config with specific IP address (10.0.6.15). No service discovery, no DNS-based resolution.
findings.gap: Hard-coded IP for database. Environment migration requires config file changes.
findings.recommendation: Use environment variables or Parameter Store. Adopt RDS DNS endpoints.

findings.title: No managed object storage
findings.description: No S3 or managed object storage. All data in on-premises SQL Server. No parsing pipeline for unstructured data.
findings.gap: No S3 or managed storage. Data locked in on-premises SQL Server.
findings.recommendation: Use S3 for document/attachment storage needs when modernizing.

findings.title: No data access layer — SQL scattered in UI handlers
findings.description: SQL queries inline in page event handlers with string-concatenated SqlCommand objects. No repository pattern, no ORM. SQL injection vulnerabilities present.
findings.gap: Database queries inline in UI handlers. No abstraction. SQL injection risk.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/data access layer with ORM (EF Core or Dapper) and parameterized queries.

findings.title: SQL Server 2005 — 10+ years past end-of-life
findings.description: SQL Server 2005 reached end of extended support in April 2016. No security patches available. No version pinning in IaC (no IaC exists).
findings.gap: Database engine 10+ years past EOL. Critical security vulnerabilities unpatched.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported SQL Server (2019/2022) on RDS or Aurora PostgreSQL.

findings.title: No encryption at rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. SQL Server 2005 does not support TDE. Data stored unencrypted.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest on the database. Sensitive employee data unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with KMS after migrating to RDS.

findings.title: Cookie-based auth without SSL — no token-based auth
findings.description: Forms authentication with cookies but no token-based auth (OAuth2/JWT). SSL not required — cookies sent in the clear.
findings.gap: No token-based authentication. Cookies transmitted without encryption.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT with Cognito. Enforce HTTPS.

findings.title: Standalone authentication with no external IdP
findings.description: Application manages authentication entirely via custom Forms Auth with Login.aspx. No centralized IdP integration, no SSO.
findings.gap: No external IdP. No SSO. Cannot participate in organizational identity policies.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or organizational IdP for centralized identity.

findings.title: Plaintext credentials in source control
findings.description: Plaintext database credentials committed in web.config: User ID=ts_app;Password=Time2006!. No Secrets Manager, no encryption, no rotation.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in version control. Critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Rotate credentials immediately. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Unpatchable OS — Windows Server 2003 EOL
findings.description: Windows Server 2003 and IIS 6 are end-of-life with no security patches since July 2015. Runtime is fundamentally unpatchable.
findings.gap: Running on unpatchable OS. No vulnerability scanning. Critical CVE exposure.
findings.recommendation: Migrate off Windows Server 2003. Use managed compute (Fargate/Lambda) to eliminate OS patching.

findings.title: No application security scanning
findings.description: No SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. No CI/CD pipeline to integrate security scanning. Known SQL injection vulnerabilities undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning. Known vulnerabilities exist undetected.
findings.recommendation: Include SAST and dependency scanning when implementing CI/CD.

findings.title: No distributed tracing
findings.description: No X-Ray, OpenTelemetry, or any tracing instrumentation. No observability of any kind.
findings.gap: No tracing. Cannot diagnose request flow issues.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with X-Ray or OpenTelemetry when rewriting.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency thresholds, no availability targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs. No way to measure service health against user expectations.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for availability and latency after migrating to AWS.

findings.title: No business metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business event tracking.
findings.gap: No business metrics. Cannot measure outcomes or usage patterns.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics for business events after modernizing.

findings.title: No anomaly detection or alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No anomaly detection, no threshold alarms. Failures detected only via user reports.
findings.gap: No alerting. Failures go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms and anomaly detection after AWS migration.

findings.title: No automated tests
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. No unit tests, no integration tests. Zero test coverage.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage. No regression safety net.
findings.recommendation: Implement integration tests for critical workflows when rewriting. Add to CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: No observability ownership
findings.description: No dashboards, no alarms with owners, no CODEOWNERS for observability. No observability artifacts exist.
findings.gap: No observability infrastructure or ownership model.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards and alarms with named owners after modernizing.

immediate_actions: Rewrite to .NET 6+ for Linux container support

pathways.name: Move to Open Source
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: DATA-Q4=4 >= 3; no stored procedures to migrate. Primary trigger not met.

triggering_questions.note: No stored procedures — no proprietary SQL coupling to migrate away from

pathways.not_triggered_reason: DATA-Q4=4 (no stored procedures). While SQL Server is a commercial database, the absence of proprietary SQL constructs means the primary trigger (DATA-Q4 < 3) is not met.

pathways.name: Move to Managed Databases
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q2=1 < 3 (self-managed SQL Server 2005). DATA-Q3=1 strengthens (EOL engine).

triggering_questions.note: SQL Server 2005 is 10+ years past EOL

immediate_actions: Choose target engine (RDS SQL Server or Aurora PostgreSQL)
